title: Procedural Tail Follow-Through Physics Chain
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that loads a horse model and attaches a procedural physics-driven tail chain that exhibits realistic follow-through and secondary animation.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 6) looking at the origin.
- Add a HemisphereLight (sky: 0x87ceeb, ground: 0x443322, intensity 1.0) and a DirectionalLight (0xffffff, intensity 1.2) at position (5, 8, 3) with shadow mapping enabled.
- Set the renderer background to 0x1a1a2e. Enable shadows on the renderer.
- Add a ground plane (PlaneGeometry 20x20, MeshStandardMaterial color 0x334455) rotated to be horizontal, at y=0, receiving shadows.
- Load 'horse.glb' using GLTFLoader from Three.js examples CDN. Scale the model to fit roughly 2 units tall. Center it at the origin.

TAIL CHAIN SYSTEM:
- After loading the horse, create a procedural tail consisting of exactly 8 chain segments (spheres, radius 0.06 each, MeshStandardMaterial color 0xff6644).
- The tail root attaches to the horse's rear (approximate position: the bounding box back-center, offset slightly up). Store this as the anchor point.
- Each segment follows the previous one using a spring-damper system:
  - Spring stiffness (k): 35.0 (adjustable)
  - Damping (d): 0.85
  - Segment rest distance: 0.18
  - Gravity: -9.81 applied to each segment's velocity
- Each segment stores position (Vector3) and velocity (Vector3). On each frame, for each segment i (0 = closest to body):
  - The target for segment 0 is the anchor point; for segment i>0 it is segment i-1's position.
  - Compute spring force toward target, apply damping, apply gravity, integrate velocity and position using delta time.
  - Clamp segment distance from its target to a max of 0.3 to prevent explosion.

HORSE MOVEMENT:
- The horse can be moved with arrow keys: Left/Right rotate the horse (yaw, 2 rad/s), Up/Down move the horse forward/backward along its facing direction (speed 2 units/s).
- The anchor point updates with the horse's world transform each frame.
- When the horse moves, the tail should naturally trail behind with follow-through physics.

SIMULATION CONTROLS:
- Add a DOM button with id 'btn-reset' labeled 'Reset' that resets the horse to origin facing +Z and snaps all tail segments to the anchor point with zero velocity.
- Add a DOM button with id 'btn-wind' labeled 'Toggle Wind' that toggles a lateral wind force of (2.0, 0, 0) applied to all tail segments. Default: wind OFF.
- Add a slider input with id 'slider-stiffness' (range 5 to 80, step 1, default 35) that adjusts the spring stiffness in real time. Display the current value in a span with id 'stiffness-value'.

HUD:
- Show an overlay div (id 'hud') in the top-left with:
  - Horse position (x, z) rounded to 2 decimals
  - Horse rotation (yaw in degrees, rounded to 1 decimal)
  - Tail tip position (last segment x, y, z rounded to 2 decimals)
  - Wind status: 'ON' or 'OFF'
  - FPS counter

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
  - horsePosition: {x, y, z} — horse world position
  - horseRotationY: number — yaw in radians
  - tailSegments: array of 8 objects each with {x, y, z, vx, vy, vz} (position and velocity)
  - tailSegmentCount: 8
  - windEnabled: boolean
  - stiffness: number (current spring stiffness)
  - anchorPosition: {x, y, z}
  - simulationTime: number (accumulated seconds)
  - fps: number
  - modelLoaded: boolean (true once horse.glb is loaded)

Style the UI controls in a panel at the bottom-center with semi-transparent dark background, white text, and rounded corners.
physics_constraints: Spring-damper chain: F_spring = -k * (pos - target_normalized * restDist), velocity *= damping per frame, gravity = -9.81 on Y axis. Segment distance from target clamped to max 0.3. All positions and velocities must remain finite (no NaN/Infinity). Tail must exhibit follow-through: when horse stops, tail continues swinging and settles.
